So I got invited a while back to share boring tales of my life by the charismatic @I-am-me. Wasn't sure what to ramble about so I waited for inspiration... it never came, so here I go anyways.

Being raised by a PhD in Psych & a an overly emotional mom (The divorce will be another post), I had the opportunity to observe two polar opposites dealing with life & kids. On the one hand I had a father totally in control of his emotions and on the other a mother whom, more often than not, let her emotions control her.

Being the last of 3 boys I had been awarded the title of mama's favorite little baby. She cuddled me whenever she could, acting as a shield against lifes inevitable unpleasantness & harsh realities. Protecting my feelings from any adversity they could encounter. She would have done anything for me, even to this day I have to respectfully decline her abundant offers for assistance where none is needed. Growing up, I went to live with her for a few years until an illness creeped up on her. During those years, I learned to listen & talk openly, I was taught that the world is made up of beautiful people & some unpleasant scum, I also learned about feelings & emotions being something we must dutifully respect about others.

That was my weakening...

So mom goes to the hospital for a few months & I'm back with dad & my 2 "brothers".

Being the 3rd kid, out of 2 desired ones, my dad dealt with me differently than my bros. He had experience by now & didn't want me to follow in their footsteps. One is a free range drug abuser and socialite, the other a textbook loner more confortable being in his room by himself.

He quickly realized how emotionally open my mom had made me and decided to toughen me up. The memories I have of him back then were that of a very serious man, dedicated to making sure we didn't lack anything but unfortunately, he seldomly took off that mask.

He taught me about how most people are slaves to their emotions, having trouble letting logic dictate the next course of action. How emotional decision making always has unpleasant backlash in some form, how energy is easily wasted with self pity and also how managing your emotions, as hard as it can be at times, should always be a priority.

Back then I wasn't sure how to mix all this together. My mom who firmly beleives that our emotions are a guide and my father who beleived that we should control them and use pure logic all the time.

Nearing my mid 30s, all this has had a chance to simmer in the pot.

Yes, our emotions are important, they help us figure out things about ourselves, they allow us to have empathy for others, to make socialy oriented decisions and they are in part what makes us human.

Controling them is just as important as knowing what to do with them. I've lived through events and dealt with situations where if I hadn't had the discipline to take a step back, analyze what was going on in my mind and take logical decisions, I would have unnecessarily prolonged my suffering and most definitely would have made very poor choices.

Suffering is not bad in and of itself, it's what strong negative emotions bring with them. Sometimes it's short lived, other times it can take us over, turn us into emotionally charged dysfunctional human beings. That's when you know you have to grab a hold of yourself & grow as a person

I don't beleive we should avoid our emotions, quite the opposite. But I also believe we should be in control of our lives, not letting feelings decide the futur for us.

So the next time you suffer from emotional turmoil, do your best to channel that energy in a way that will help you grow stronger, tougher & be better prepared for futur dealings with the scum that surrounds us. Everone suffers, not everyone is prepared to deal with it in a healthy way. So don't be a prick to someone who doesn't have as big tool chest like yours for dealing with life.

Am I making sense here ?
Suffering is inevitable, how you channel that energy is up to you.
